answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates from an honest anchor through a bounded-length random walk, so each node’s influence decays with distance and mixing time. A sybil cluster isolated behind a sparse external cut has low conductance; by conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds, only limited stationary probability crosses its boundary, mathematically capping the cluster’s aggregate voting weight. Thus no quill can redraw the trust horizon unobserved.
